[[File:LindnerAttractor.webm|thumb|Delay coordinate embedding attractor reconstruction of the strange nonchaotic dynamics of the pulsating star KIC 5520878]]

In mathematics, a '''strange nonchaotic attractor''' ('''SNA''') is a form of [[attractor]] which, while converging to a limit, is [[strange attractor#Strange attractor|strange]], because it is not [[piecewise differentiable]], and also non-[[chaos theory|chaotic]], in that its [[Lyapunov exponents]] are non-positive.<ref name=alseda>{{cite web|url=http://mat.uab.cat/~alseda/talks/SNA_Defin20070308.pdf|title=On the definition of Strange Nonchaotic Attractor|author=Lluís Alsedà|date=March 8, 2007|access-date=2014-05-07}}</ref> SNAs were introduced as a topic of study by Grebogi et al. in 1984.<ref name=alseda/><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Grebogi | first1=Celso | last2=Ott | first2=Edward | last3=Pelikan | first3=Steven | last4=Yorke | first4=James A. | title=Strange attractors that are not chaotic | journal=Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=13 | issue=1–2 | year=1984 | issn=0167-2789 | doi=10.1016/0167-2789(84)90282-3 | pages=261–268| bibcode=1984PhyD...13..261G }}</ref> SNAs can be distinguished from [[periodic attractor|periodic]], [[quasiperiodic]] and [[chaotic attractor]]s using the [[0-1 test for chaos]].<ref>{{cite journal|arxiv=1303.0169|last1= Gopal|first1= R.|title= Applicability of 0-1 Test for Strange Nonchaotic Attractors|last2=  Venkatesan|first2= A.|last3=  Lakshmanan|first3= M.|year= 2013|doi=10.1063/1.4808254|pmid= 23822488|volume=23|issue= 2|journal=Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science|page=023123|bibcode=2013Chaos..23b3123G}}</ref>

Periodically driven damped nonlinear systems can exhibit complex dynamics characterized by strange chaotic attractors, where strange refers  to  the  fractal  geometry of the attractor and chaotic refers to the exponential sensitivity of orbits on the attractor. Quasiperiodically driven systems forced by incommensurate frequencies are natural extensions of periodically driven ones and are phenomenologically richer. In addition to periodic or quasiperiodic motion, they can exhibit chaotic or nonchaotic motion on strange  attractors. Although quasiperiodic forcing is not necessary for strange nonchaotic  dynamics (e.g., the period doubling accumulation point of a period doubling cascade), if quasiperiodic driving is not present, strange nonchaotic attractors are typically not robust and not expected to occur naturally because they exist only when the system is carefully tuned to a precise critical parameter value.  On the other hand, it was shown in the paper of Grebogi et al. that SNAs can be robust when the system is quasiperiodically driven. The  first  experiment  to  demonstrate a robust strange nonchaotic attractor involved  the  buckling of a magnetoelastic ribbon driven quasiperiodically by two incommensurate frequencies in the golden ratio.<ref>{{cite journal|author1-link=William Ditto | last1=Ditto | first1=W. L. | last2=Spano | first2=M. L. | last3=Savage | first3=H. T. | last4=Rauseo | first4=S. N. | last5=Heagy | first5=J. | last6=Ott | first6=E. | title=Experimental observation of a strange nonchaotic attractor | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=65 | issue=5 | date=1990-07-30 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.65.533 | pages=533–536| pmid=10042947 | bibcode=1990PhRvL..65..533D }}</ref> Strange nonchaotic attractors have been robustly observed in laboratory experiments involving magnetoelastic ribbons, electrochemical cells, electronic circuits, and a neon glow discharge. In 2015, strange nonchaotic dynamics were identified for the pulsating [[RR Lyrae variable]] KIC 5520878, as well as three similar stars observed by the [[Kepler space telescope]], which oscillate in two frequency modes that are nearly in the [[golden ratio]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Lindner | first1=John F. | last2=Kohar | first2=Vivek | last3=Kia | first3=Behnam | last4=Hippke | first4=Michael | last5=Learned | first5=John G. | last6=Ditto | first6=William L. | title=Strange Nonchaotic Stars | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=114 | issue=5 | date=2015-02-03 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.114.054101 | article-number=054101| doi-access=free | pmid=25699444 | arxiv=1501.01747 | bibcode=2015PhRvL.114e4101L }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Applied Chaos Laboratory|url=http://appliedchaoslab.phys.hawaii.edu|website=appliedchaoslab.phys.hawaii.edu}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Strange Stars Pulsate According to the Golden Ratio|url=http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/strange-stars-pulsate-according-to-the-golden-ratio/|publisher=Scientific American|author= Clara Moskowitz|author-link= Clara Moskowitz |date=2015-02-09|access-date=2020-01-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Stars That Act Irrational|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=114|issue=5|article-number=054101|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.054101|pmid=25699444|bibcode=2015PhRvL.114e4101L|last1=Lindner|first1=John F.|last2=Kohar|first2=Vivek|last3=Kia|first3=Behnam|last4=Hippke|first4=Michael|last5=Learned|first5=John G.|last6=Ditto|first6=William L.|year=2015|arxiv=1501.01747}}</ref>
